## Hands-on 1 – The setup check {#hands-on-1-the-setup-check .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 1 – the setup check.** Get to the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you.

- **Workspace:** your IDE opens the workspace folder, and `source("R/check_setup.R")` prints an `[OK]` line for every check; the last one fits a number that you will meet again later, `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 4)` points of distrust per point of concern
- **Then, while you are online:** `source("R/spec_tools.R"); fetch_multi100()` downloads the file of Task 3 (29 MB) once and checks it
- **Browser lab:** the page has finished loading, and the setup cell reports `r fmt_n(nrow(ess))` respondents and the same `r fmt_num(curve_ref$b, 4)`
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Take the time you need, **into the break** if necessary. Type a green circle in chat when you are through; type **STUCK** and I will come to you.
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
If your installation will not cooperate, do not fight it – open the browser lab and follow along. It is a demonstration: every task is there with its results already computed, and both of your submissions work, but it fits nothing of your own.
:::

::: notes
Your turn, and this first task is deliberately not intellectual. The job is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. In the workspace, open the folder in your IDE and source the check script: it prints one OK line for each thing that the course needs, and the last check fits a model and prints a number that you will meet again later. Then, while the network is good, run the second line on the slide, which downloads the file that the analysts received and that we need after lunch. In the browser lab, which shows every task with its results already computed, wait for the page, run the setup cell, and check the two numbers. Take the time you need, into the break if you have to. A green circle in chat when you are through, STUCK if you need me.
:::
